entries.summary: Sunday 17:06 EST: Bearish — Elevated Downside Risk remains the November 23–25 base case. Fresh November 22 Reuters correction analysis and Barron's strategist review present competing oversold-rebound and further-liquidation scenarios, without a verified new US cash-session response or material change from the 15:40 EST assessment. Friday's semiconductor-led liquidation remains the dominant confirmed signal. Sunday futures direction is secondary and unsynchronized. Curated Open Watch remains unchanged since November 21 00:44 UTC. Synchronized VXN/VIX, Treasury 10Y/2Y, CME FedWatch and contract-matched oil are not independently verified.

editorial.marketOverview: The November 23–25 base case remains elevated downside risk after Friday's severe semiconductor-led US equity liquidation. Reuters' November 22 correction analysis notes valuation relief and possible bottoming signals but also persistent AI infrastructure-spending doubts and weak breadth. Friday's closes are historical, not new Sunday prices.
editorial.whatChanged: Relative to the repository's Sunday 15:40 EST assessment, no verified new curated Open Watch catalyst or synchronized US cash-market response changes the directional call. Barron's November 22 strategist commentary offers medium-term recovery arguments and acknowledges potential further losses. These are analyst views, not realized price action.
editorial.marketInterpretation: QQQ/Nasdaq and SOX weakness together with negative breadth favor defensive interpretation. Oversold conditions and tentative futures support may generate a sharp countertrend bounce, but futures indications lack contract/timestamp verification. The Friday VIX closing discrepancy (35.89 Reuters versus 37.66 Barron's) remains unresolved; VXN is unavailable. Treasury 10Y 4.93% and 2Y 4.65% are unsynchronized and must not be combined into a fresh spread; the historical 29 bp spread used prior 4.94% and 4.65%. Friday WTI $83.98 and Brent $92.57 per barrel are historical settlements, not contemporaneous Sunday oil reactions. CME FedWatch probabilities are unavailable; avoid invented probabilities.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday November 23: expect high-volatility price discovery, with the key test whether QQQ and SOX/SMH stabilize together following Friday's liquidation and flash PMIs. Tuesday November 24: consumer confidence and technology earnings could validate a bounce or renew de-risking. Wednesday November 25: the scheduled inflation/growth data cluster and Beige Book raise event risk. These are conditional paths, not forecast realized returns.
editorial.bullCase: A credible recovery requires simultaneous QQQ/Nasdaq and SOX/SMH strength, improving advance-decline breadth and falling VXN/VIX across matched timestamps. Cooling Treasury yields without deteriorating growth expectations, reassuring earnings and softer-than-feared inflation would strengthen the rebound case. None is yet verified for Monday's cash session.
editorial.bearCase: A failed rebound with continued semiconductor underperformance, negative breadth, sustained volatility and oil/rate pressure would confirm downside continuation. NVDA legal/accounting headlines and regional security risks compound fragility, but new announcements must be distinguished from established misconduct or proven US-market effects.
editorial.watchNext: Verify Monday US opening and closing QQQ, Nasdaq, SOX, SMH, breadth and VXN/VIX at matched timestamps; obtain direct contemporaneous 10Y/2Y yields, CME probabilities and oil contract/expiry details. Monitor November 23 flash PMIs, November 24 confidence/earnings and November 25 data releases, plus curated Open Watch changes and primary issuer/regulator updates.
